tasks.title: Fix a binary search
tasks.prompt:
This Python function has bugs:

```python
def first_at_least(xs, target):
    """Return the index of the first element >= target in the sorted list xs, or len(xs) if there is none."""
    lo, hi = 0, len(xs) - 1
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if xs[mid] < target:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    return lo
```

Fix it (keep the name and the signature, do not use the bisect module) and return the complete corrected function in one python block.

check.tests:
import random, bisect
assert first_at_least([1,3,3,5],3)==1
assert first_at_least([1,3,5],4)==2
assert first_at_least([],1)==0
assert first_at_least([1,2],5)==2
assert first_at_least([1,2],0)==0
random.seed(7)
for _ in range(300):
    xs=sorted(random.randint(0,20) for _ in range(random.randint(0,15)))
    t=random.randint(-2,22)
    assert first_at_least(xs,t)==bisect.bisect_left(xs,t),(xs,t)

tasks.title: Expression evaluator
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function evaluate(expr) that evaluates an arithmetic expression with integers, + - * /, parentheses and unary minus, with the usual precedence and left associativity. / is true division. Spaces may appear anywhere. Raise ValueError for malformed input such as '2+' or '(1'. Do not use eval, exec or compile. Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
src=open(__file__,encoding='utf-8').read().split('# --- tests ---')[0]
assert 'eval(' not in src and 'exec(' not in src and 'compile(' not in src, 'uses eval/exec/compile'
assert evaluate('2+3*4')==14
assert evaluate('(2+3)*4')==20
assert evaluate('-(2+3)*2')==-10
assert evaluate('10/4')==2.5
assert evaluate('2*(3+(4-1))')==12
assert evaluate('2--3')==5
assert evaluate('  7 ')==7
assert evaluate('3-2-1')==0
assert evaluate('8/2/2')==2
for bad in ['2+','(1','','1 2','*3']:
    try:
        evaluate(bad)
        raise SystemExit('no ValueError for '+repr(bad))
    except ValueError:
        pass

tasks.title: Topological order
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function order(deps) where deps is a dict mapping a task name to a list of tasks that must come before it. Return a list of all tasks (including tasks that only appear as prerequisites) such that every prerequisite comes before the task. Whenever several tasks are available, take the alphabetically smallest one first. Raise ValueError if there is a cycle. Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
assert order({'b':['a'],'c':['a'],'d':['b','c']})==['a','b','c','d']
assert order({'x':['z'],'y':[]})==['y','z','x']
assert order({})==[]
assert order({'c':['b'],'b':['a'],'e':[]})==['a','b','c','e']
try:
    order({'a':['b'],'b':['a']})
    raise SystemExit('no ValueError for a cycle')
except ValueError:
    pass

tasks.title: Word wrap
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function wrap(text, width) that wraps text greedily into lines of at most width characters and returns the list of lines. Words are separated by any whitespace; lines are joined with single spaces and have no leading or trailing spaces. A word longer than width is split into pieces of exactly width characters (the last piece may be shorter). An empty text gives []. Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
assert wrap('the quick brown fox', 10)==['the quick','brown fox']
assert wrap('abcdefghij', 4)==['abcd','efgh','ij']
assert wrap('', 5)==[]
assert wrap('a bb ccc', 3)==['a','bb','ccc']
assert wrap('hi   there', 20)==['hi there']
assert wrap('one two three four', 9)==['one two','three','four']

tasks.title: Longest common subsequence
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function lcs(a, b) that returns one longest common subsequence of the strings a and b (any one if there are several). Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
def sub(s,t):
    it=iter(t)
    return all(ch in it for ch in s)
r=lcs('ABCBDAB','BDCABA')
assert len(r)==4 and sub(r,'ABCBDAB') and sub(r,'BDCABA'),r
assert lcs('','x')==''
assert lcs('abc','abc')=='abc'
assert lcs('abc','def')==''
r=lcs('AGGTAB','GXTXAYB')
assert len(r)==4 and sub(r,'AGGTAB') and sub(r,'GXTXAYB'),r

tasks.title: INI parser
tasks.prompt: Write a Python function parse_ini(text) that returns a dict of sections, each a dict of key -> value (strings). Rules: a line '[name]' starts a section; 'key = value' sets a value (strip spaces around key and value); a value wrapped in double quotes has the quotes removed; full-line comments start with ';' or '#'; blank lines are ignored; keys before the first section go into the section ''; a repeated key keeps the last value. Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
t='a = 1
; c
[db]
host = localhost 
port=5432
# x

name = "my app"
[db]
port = 6543
[empty]
'
d=parse_ini(t)
assert d['']=={'a':'1'},d
assert d['db']=={'host':'localhost','port':'6543','name':'my app'},d
assert d['empty']=={},d
assert parse_ini('')=={} or parse_ini('')=={'':{}}

tasks.title: Sliding-window rate limiter
tasks.prompt: Write a Python class RateLimiter(limit, window) with a method allow(t) where t is a timestamp in seconds (calls come with non-decreasing t). allow returns True and counts the call if fewer than limit calls were allowed in the half-open window (t - window, t]; otherwise it returns False and the call does not count. Only the code in one python block.

check.tests:
rl=RateLimiter(2,10)
assert rl.allow(0) is True
assert rl.allow(1) is True
assert rl.allow(2) is False
assert rl.allow(10) is True
assert rl.allow(10.5) is False
assert rl.allow(11.1) is True
r2=RateLimiter(1,5)
assert [r2.allow(x) for x in [0,4,5,9.9,10]]==[True,False,True,False,True]
